newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Jan-Oct non-energy exports at $688 mln.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Jan-Oct non-energy exports at $688 mln.

text.p: Algeria's non-energy exports reached $688 million in the first 10 months of 1996, Finance Minister Abdelkrim Harchaoui said on Monday.

Harchaoui made the announcement while addressing Algeria's National Transitional Council -- the country's quasi-parliament, the official Algerian news agency reported. The council is examining the government's 1997 draft budget, already approved by the cabinet.
"Algeria's non-energy exports reached $688 million during the first ten months of the year," APS quoted Harchaoui as saying. It gave no comparative figures for the year-earlier period.

Non-energy exports went to 28 countries during the January to October period. Exports to Russia represented 50 percent of the total, "in the framework of repayment of Algeria's debt," APS said without providing further details. About 33 percent of the total went to the European Union.

Algeria, a member of OPEC, relies on oil and natural gas sales for nearly 95 percent of its foreign income. Much of its state-owned industry outside the energy sector operates at less than 50 percent of capacity.
The government's budget assumes $11.1 billion in income from hydrocarbon exports next year.
